name: chicken tenders
instructions:
Breaded chicken tenders. Two variants on the adhesive layer that binds the breadcrumbs to the chicken: variant A uses the classical FLOUR + EGG YOLK dredge; variant B uses MAYO + DIJON MUSTARD (borrowed from what would have been the breadcrumb-tofu approach — mayo works well on chicken too, and skips the separate egg step). Same seasoned-breadcrumb coat and bake/fry finish for both.

SHARED PREP:
- Cut chicken breast into TENDER-SIZED STRIPS (or use pre-cut chicken tenders). Chicken thighs also work but need to be trimmed into strips.
- Season the BREADCRUMBS, not the chicken (see notes). REGULAR breadcrumbs (fine crumb — see PANKO note; schnitzel uses panko instead). Standard stack: salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, herbes de provence, dried oregano — mix into the breadcrumbs first so it distributes.

=== VARIANT A — FLOUR + EGG YOLK ADHESIVE (CLASSICAL DREDGE) ===

1. Dust each strip in all-purpose flour, shaking off excess. The flour gives the egg yolk something to grip.
2. Dip in beaten EGG YOLK (yolk only — not whole egg; see notes) until fully coated.
3. Press into the seasoned breadcrumbs until evenly covered.

=== VARIANT B — POTATO STARCH + MAYO/DIJON WASH + BREADCRUMBS ===

1. Dust each strip in POTATO STARCH, shaking off excess (starch dredge instead of flour).
2. Wash with a thin layer of MAYONNAISE + DIJON MUSTARD (in place of the egg yolk). Mayo gives fat and structure; dijon adds tang.
3. Press into the seasoned breadcrumbs until evenly covered.

Same three-step shape as variant A (dredge → wash → coat) with starch swapped for flour and mayo/dijon swapped for egg yolk.

=== SHARED FINISH ===

1. Spray or drizzle AVOCADO OIL over the breaded strips (crisps the crust; high smoke point handles the bake temp).
2. BAKE at ~425°F until the breadcrumbs are deeply golden and the chicken is cooked through, OR pan-fry in a thin layer of oil for a deeper crust.

=== BEST PAIRING — FREEZER FRIES ===

Best reason to buy freezer fries. Bake them alongside the tenders (same oven, similar temp, similar time). Classic chicken-tenders-and-fries plate. See notes.
notes:
Combined from two earlier files (breadcrumb-chicken + breadcrumb-tofu). Both were unattempted separately; merged into a chicken-tenders format because that's the actual dish I want to make, with the mayo-adhesive path preserved as a second variant.

=== TWO ADHESIVE VARIANTS — WHY BOTH WORK ===

VARIANT A — FLOUR + EGG YOLK: the classical three-step dredge (flour → egg → breadcrumbs). Chicken has surface protein and moisture that grip flour cleanly; egg yolk (not whole egg — see below) gives the richest fat and deepest golden crust.

VARIANT B — POTATO STARCH + MAYO/DIJON WASH + BREADCRUMBS: same three-step shape as variant A, with starch swapped for flour and mayo/dijon swapped for egg yolk. The mayo/dijon idea was originally captured for tofu (dry surface can't grip a plain flour-and-egg dredge alone); works on chicken too. Advantages: dijon adds a real flavor layer (tang + mustard depth) that variant A doesn't have; potato starch gives an extra-crispy crust (starch fries crispier than flour). Tradeoff: variant B reads slightly more of the mayo/mustard on the finished piece, which competes with heavily-seasoned breadcrumbs. Variant A stays cleaner and lets the breadcrumb seasoning lead.

PICK BY WHAT YOU'RE GOING FOR: cleaner classical crust → variant A. Extra tang + crispier starch-based crust → variant B.

=== YOLK ONLY, NOT WHOLE EGG (VARIANT A) ===

Egg yolk gives the richest fat content and the deepest-golden crust. Whole egg dilutes the yolk's binding power with whites (which set rubbery in the bake). Egg whites alone don't have the fat needed for a real crust. Yolk-only is the upgrade move.

=== SEASON THE BREADCRUMBS, NOT THE CHICKEN ===

Seasoning the chicken before the breading traps flavor under the coat where you can't taste it. Seasoning the breadcrumbs puts the flavor on the outside where it lands on your tongue first. Applies to both variants. Standard stack: salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, herbes de provence, dried oregano — mix into the breadcrumbs thoroughly before dredging.

Composite breadcrumb blends (lemon-pepper-breadcrumbs, pine-nut-breadcrumbs, deviled-breadcrumbs, massaman-breadcrumbs) can also be used in place of plain-panko + separate seasonings. Cross-reference those recipes.

=== REGULAR BREADCRUMBS OVER PANKO — SCHNITZEL GETS THE PANKO ===

Use REGULAR / FINE breadcrumbs here (not panko). Fine breadcrumbs give a softer, more classical-american-tender crumb texture. Panko's larger, drier flakes read too aggressively crunchy for the tenders format — that texture belongs on chicken-schnitzel (see that sibling recipe). Different crust registers on the same breading family; schnitzel wants the crunch, tenders wants the crumb.

=== AVOCADO OIL SPRAY ON TOP ===

A spray or drizzle of avocado oil before baking crisps the breadcrumbs into a real crust. High smoke point matters because the bake temp wants to be hot (425°F). Olive oil burns at that temp; vegetable oil is fine if no avocado on hand.

=== TENDER-SIZED STRIPS, NOT WHOLE CUTLETS ===

Cut chicken breast into strips (or use pre-cut tenders). Whole cutlets work but need to be pounded to even thickness first and take longer to cook — tenders are the faster, more shareable format. Chicken thighs also work as tender strips; trim the excess fat first.

=== BAKE OR PAN-FRY ===

Bake is hands-off and lets you cook a bunch at once alongside the fries. Pan-fry gives a deeper, browner crust but you have to babysit it and cook in batches. Pick by whether you want the hands-off tray bake or the deeper crust.

=== BEST PAIRING — FREEZER FRIES ===

Best reason to buy freezer fries. The chicken-tenders-and-fries plate is what this recipe is really for — bake the fries on a separate tray in the same oven, at the same 425°F temp, in roughly the same time window. Fries take slightly longer to crisp; pull the tenders when they're done and give the fries a few extra minutes if needed. Homemade fries are better but a lot more work; freezer fries pair with tenders cleanly enough that the effort tradeoff usually isn't worth it.

=== DIPPING SAUCES — HONEY / BARBECUE (NOT TARTAR) ===

Chicken tenders favor sweet-forward dips — HONEY and BARBECUE SAUCE are the canonical picks. Also fine: honey mustard (mix honey + dijon), ranch, ketchup.

WHY NOT TARTAR SAUCE: tartar sauce (dill + pickle + capers + dill + lemon; see tartar-sauce) reads wrong against the standard tenders-and-fries american-comfort register. That's a schnitzel dip — see chicken-schnitzel. Same breaded-chicken shape, different dip axis.

=== HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM CHICKEN-PICCATA ===

chicken-piccata is the SKILLET-format cousin of this recipe. Key differences:
- FORMAT: piccata is skillet-fry (crispier crust); tenders is tray-bake (hands-off, cook a bunch at once).
- CHICKEN CUT: piccata pounds breasts to 1/4-inch cutlets; tenders cuts breasts into strips.
- COOKING METHOD: piccata's fast hot fry means chicken often isn't cooked through — needs an oven-hold + broth-based pan sauce as a light finishing braise. Tenders bake through evenly in the oven, no finish braise.
- SAUCE: piccata has a lemon-butter-caper pan sauce built into the recipe; tenders is served plain (or with dip on the side).
- ITALIAN-SWING POTENTIAL: piccata's frying-oil step opens the door to italian aromatic additions (garlic, cream) that swing the register. Tenders has no equivalent flavor-add step. NOTE: sautéed vegetables in the pan are OUT for piccata too — the point of piccata is specifically to skip the stew-factory vegetable base.

Reach for piccata when you want the skillet crust + sauce experience. Reach for tenders when you want easy hands-off + freezer fries.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- chicken-piccata: skillet-format sibling. See HOW THIS DIFFERS section above.
- lemon-pepper-breadcrumbs / pine-nut-breadcrumbs / deviled-breadcrumbs / massaman-breadcrumbs — composite breadcrumb blends usable in place of plain-panko + separate seasonings.
- breadcrumb-leeks — same breadcrumb-coating technique applied to leeks.
